Remember one line: primary and secondary teachers teach knowledge, while university teachers teach how knowledge is created. The classroom is only half the job; the other half is in laboratories and papers.
It does not suit people who only want stable classroom teaching. Universities are no longer relaxed environments, and research assessments and grant competition tighten year after year.

A common path is: bachelor's degree in psychology → master's / doctorate, with research universities generally requiring a doctorate → postdoctoral or overseas experience adds value → university recruitment → begin as lecturer, build publications and grants, and seek promotion to associate professor and professor.
This career suits people who genuinely enjoy research, are willing to teach, and can tolerate academic solitude. If reading a paper until midnight keeps you engaged, there is a place for you.

Psychology Teachers, Postsecondary teach psychology courses at universities and vocational colleges while conducting research, guiding graduate and undergraduate students, supporting academic service, and promoting public knowledge.

paragraphs: On a teaching day, deliver two consecutive morning classes and answer questions about graduate school and research topics between sessions. In the afternoon, hold a lab meeting, hear student progress, and discuss the next experiment. On a research day, recruit participants in the lab or analyze data, revise manuscripts, and write grants in the office. Near assessment season, also count outputs and complete forms.

In one line: teach well, produce research, and develop students. Duties include instruction, research design and papers, grant applications, graduate mentoring, academic service, and discipline development.

AI can write a literature review in ten minutes, but teachers still provide the academic judgment on whether a research design is sound and how to mentor a student.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 52,500 postsecondary psychology teachers were employed in 2024, rising to a projected 54,400 by 2034, a net increase of about 1,900 jobs, with approximately 4,000 openings annually. Median annual pay was about $80,300 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace postsecondary psychology teachers, but it will take over repetitive teaching preparation and research tasks. AI increasingly handles slide generation, literature organization, data analysis, and first drafts. Classroom teaching, research design, academic judgment, and student mentoring remain human strengths that machines cannot replace.

Research-design judgment: selecting the right statistical method and determining whether an experiment can test the hypothesis are core skills.
Classroom teaching: making students' eyes light up while explaining abstract theory depends on live communication.
Student mentoring: revising papers, guiding experiments, and easing academic anxiety require one-on-one expertise.
Academic ethics and judgment: people must decide how far data can be used and how strongly conclusions can be stated.
Disciplinary perspective: connecting fragmented studies into a coherent system requires academic intuition built over time.

paragraphs: A score of 5/10 reflects the occupation's substantial literature, statistics, and writing workload, which AI is rapidly taking over.

Moderately high exposure does not mean high risk. AI makes research easier to begin, shifting value toward judgment and creativity. Choosing the right topic, designing a sound study, and defending conclusions depend on human academic expertise. Formulaic, low-value publishing faces pressure, while rigorous researchers become scarcer.

Prepare for doctoral study if you want a university career; research universities generally require a doctorate plus overseas experience. Choose a direction early in graduate school and join projects. Do not focus only on the imagined ease of teaching, because academia is a marathon.

Use AI for literature, statistics, and writing, leaving time for high-quality research and student mentoring. While meeting assessment targets, commit deeply to one direction capable of producing genuine results rather than spreading effort widely.

Applied psychology and mental health roles are expanding and offer relatively accessible university entry. Candidates with industry experience in business or counseling have distinct advantages as applied instructors. Emphasize achievements in courses, research projects, and mentoring.

Do not hire teachers solely by publication count; assess academic judgment and teaching potential. Ask candidates to explain a research design they want to pursue but have not yet conducted. Comprehensive talent that teaches, researches, and mentors students deserves the greatest investment.

This career suits people curious about the human mind who also enjoy the classroom. You want to understand how people work and explain the answers to others.

The most grounded satisfaction comes from witnessing student growth. A student whose eyes light up in a first-year class returns years later with an original research project to discuss. You teach not only knowledge but a way of seeing problems.
Investigative I + Artistic A + Social S
If you accept vacations without real vacations and are willing to stay up late for one paper or one student, this career likely suits you.

paragraphs: The greatest career risk is not AI but hollow scholarship under assessment pressure. Chasing trends and producing shallow papers creates neither genuine results nor lasting competitiveness; solid research in the right direction is the long-term moat.

paragraphs: Eliminated by AI and institutional pressure

AI can generate polished literature reviews and statistical charts, but a student sitting in your office saying they do not know whether to continue graduate school needs more than information. That guidance cannot be replaced by a machine and is a reason this occupation exists.
